name: Donkey kick
movement: one bent leg lifted until the thigh is in line with the back

phone.placement: Lay the phone on its side on the floor, two or three metres away, side on to where you will be.

words.hint: Phone on its side on the floor, side on to you, on your hands and knees, whole body in frame.
words.start: Lay the phone on its side on the floor, then get on your hands and knees side on to it, and kick one leg up.
words.position: On your hands and knees, side on to the phone, hands under your shoulders, knees under your hips, back flat.
words.top: The working thigh in line with the back, knee still bent at a right angle, back flat and still.
howto: Hands under the shoulders, knees under the hips, back flat, neck long, eyes to the floor.
Keeping the knee bent at a right angle, lift the leg nearest the camera, sole to the ceiling, until the thigh is in line with the back.
Hold at the top for the count without arching the lower back or rocking the trunk to make height.
Lower slowly to the floor — the rep counts there. Sets alternate legs.
words.cannot: The shape of the spine — a sag or a round — the hips rolling open toward the working side, and the far leg: it judges the arms, the trunk staying still and the lifted leg from the side. Keep your weight centred and your hips square yourself.
words.about: Donkey kick — on hands and knees, side on: the arms plumb from the floor, 85–105°, elbows straight (at least 165°); the trunk still, the hip-to-shoulder line within ±8° of where it was at the start; the working knee at a right angle, 80–100°; and the lift, the angle at the hip between knee and shoulder, at least 165° at the top and no more than 8° above the line of the back. Hold two seconds at the top, lower slowly, and the rep counts when the knee is back down. One leg per set, the sets alternating.
words.lost: Get onto your hands and knees, side on to the camera
words.early: Hold it at the top next time
words.safety: Height comes from the hip, never from arching the lower back. Stop if the back or the wrists hurt.
words.easier: A smaller lift; a shorter hold; forearms down instead of hands.
words.harder: A band around the thighs; an ankle weight; a longer hold at the top.
words.mistakes: Arching the lower back to lift higher; rocking the trunk; the knee straightening; the shoulders drifting behind the wrists; the head dropping.

measurements.label: knee angle
measurements.why: The working knee stays at a right angle.

measurements.label: knee, hip, shoulder

settings.label: Lift at the top, at least

measurements.why: The lift: the angle at the hip between the knee and the shoulder, about 90–115 kneeling, 180 with the thigh in line with the back, read on past it, so a thigh kicked above the back keeps rising rather than reading as one coming down. Also the progress measurement.

measurements.label: thigh above the back

settings.label: Thigh above the back, at most

measurements.why: The thigh's rise over the back's line: the knee above the hip plus the shoulder above the hip is zero when the three are in a line, positive when the knee is past it — the lower back arching to make height.

measurements.label: arm from the floor
measurements.why: The wrist-to-shoulder line from the floor: 90 plumb, over 90 the shoulders are ahead of the wrists (toward the head), under it behind them.

measurements.label: trunk still

settings.label: Trunk tilted from the start, at most (degrees)

measurements.why: The hip-to-shoulder line, as its change since the start: rocking back onto the knees reads up, rocking forward or the hips dropping toward the kicking side reads down. There is no landmark on the spine, so a sag or a round is not seen — the trunk moving is.

faults.label: Shoulders behind wrists
faults.deep: Shoulders forward — you are sitting back on your heels

faults.label: Shoulders ahead of wrists
faults.deep: Shoulders back — they are well ahead of your wrists

faults.label: Elbows bent
faults.deep: Straighten your arms — the elbows are well bent

faults.label: Rocking back
faults.text: Keep your trunk still — weight over hands and knees
faults.deep: Stay still — you are rocking back onto your knees

faults.label: Rocking forward
faults.deep: Stay still — you are rocking forward onto your hands

faults.label: Knee straightening
faults.text: Keep the knee bent — sole to the ceiling
faults.deep: Bend the knee to a right angle — the leg is straightening

faults.label: Knee too closed
faults.deep: Open the knee out to a right angle

faults.label: Thigh above back
faults.text: Not so high — thigh in line with your back
faults.deep: Lower it — the thigh is past your back and the back is arching

faults.label: Thigh short of the line
faults.text: Lift higher — thigh level with your back
faults.deep: Higher — knee, hip and shoulder in one line

settings.label: Hip angle that counts as a kick
